summary: A supervisor meeting a team asks what motivates each person and what they want from a leader before laying out rules.
realLife: A university HR guide tells new managers to hold an introduction meeting, ask staff what motivates them, and say how they plan to lead through one-on-ones and open talk.
sources: University of Toledo HR, Manager's First Week guide: https://www.utoledo.edu/depts/hr/training-and-organizational-development/docs/Manager-Week-One.pdf
inGame: the person's job record (employer, position, workplace) and the new-coworker event carry who and where; the speaker's habit is a line choice by trait; needs: a recorded orientation or training session

turns.summary: The supervisor reads the rules and expectations first and asks nothing.
turns.writesBack: a cooler tie; the newcomer notes feeling talked at

turns.summary: The supervisor asks, nods, and never mentions it again.
turns.writesBack: a promise left unkept in the journal as a mild mood drop

turns.summary: The supervisor brings up the newcomer's answer a week later.
turns.writesBack: a tie rises; a kept small promise
